neighbours.label: the subject or adverb right before a verb of lying at rest (there he lay, it now lies): a context that predicts 'lie/lay' rather than 'stand/sit'
fire: The old horse collapsed in the field, and there it lay until morning.
The wreck was scuttled in 1971 and now lies in forty metres of water.
Struck by the falling branch, he dropped, and there he lay for an hour.
The ancient king was buried under the hill, where he still lies today.
She fainted on the stairs and there she lay until a neighbour came.
The fallen statue toppled into the river, where it lies half buried.
The injured climber slipped into the crevasse and there he lay all night.
The galleon sank in a storm in 1622 and today it lies off the Florida coast.
quiet: The old horse recovered in the field, and there it stood until morning.
The tower was restored in 1971 and now stands in the middle of the square.
Pleased with the speech, he rose, and there he stood for an hour.
The ancient king was crowned in the hall, where his throne still stands today.
She waited at the table and there she sat until a neighbour came.
The bronze statue was raised beside the river, where it stands proudly.
The tired climber reached the summit and there he stood all morning.
The lighthouse was built in 1622 and today it stands on the Florida coast.

predictions: fire 0.2-0.5 on the token before 'lay/lies' when the context sets up lying; stand/sit contexts below 0.05
notes: Card: - pole promotes lie/lying/laid (the + pole promotes stand); peaks on ' he', ' she', ' just', ' now' before lie/lay. Probe: 'fell and there he lay' 0.458, 'sunk ... now lies' 0.224, 'Lie on your back' 0.209; 'stand tall' 0.011, 'stood at the gate' 0.006, 'went home and lay down' 0.096.
